mainTopic: שירה over נסכים alone, and dating the first חורבן
overview: The גמרא asks whether נסכים brought without a קרבן need the לויים' שירה. It tries to prove that they do from רבי יוסי's ברייתא: the לויים were singing when the first בית המקדש was destroyed, and the only thing they could have been singing over was נסכים. רבא (or רב אשי) rejects the proof, because the פסוק they sang was not that day's שיר. It was only a lament that came into their mouths. Standing on the דוכן proves nothing either, because ריש לקיש allows singing without a קרבן. They still did not sing over נסכים alone, out of worry that people would treat the required שירה as optional. The גמרא then turns to the ברייתא itself and asks how the first חורבן could have been in the year after שביעית, since a פסוק in יחזקאל places a יובל fourteen years later. רבינא answers that the fourteen years start after the year of the destruction. A back-and-forth over the 'twenty-fifth year of our exile' follows. It ends with the explanation that there were only two exiles, dated from two starting points, and the supporting timeline of נבוכדנצר's reign begins at the end of the amud.

steps.title: Do libations brought alone need song?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether נסכים that come without a קרבן require the לויים' שירה, and lays out both sides of the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: wine libations that are brought by themselves, do they need song or not? Maybe, since רבי יונתן said song is said only over wine, we say it over wine even when it is alone. Or maybe we say song only when the מזבח has both 'eating and drinking,' but not over 'drinking' alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: if wine נסכים are poured on the מזבח with no animal קרבן, do the לויים sing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן taught that שירה is said only over wine. One side reads this as 'wine is the trigger for שירה,' so wine alone would be enough. The other side reads it as 'wine is necessary but not enough': you need the full meal of the מזבח, meaning the meat (eating) together with the wine (drinking).

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)
Wine libations poured on the מזבח
By themselves, without an animal קרבן
Require the לויים' song
'Eating and drinking': the קרבן's meat and the wine together

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that שירה needs wine. The only question is whether wine without a קרבן is enough.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Libations that come by themselves
do they require song
or do they not require song?
Since Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
"From where do we know that song is not said
except over the wine"
do we say it here?
phrases.notes: The idea: since wine is what brings on שירה, maybe wine alone is enough.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא עַל אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה אָמְרִינַן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps over eating and drinking we say it,
phrases.notes: 'Eating' is the קרבן burned on the מזבח, and 'drinking' is the wine poured on it.

phrases.english: but over drinking alone we do not say it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether נסכים brought without a קרבן require שירה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question in the sugya.

steps.title: Bringing in רבי יוסי's teaching about the day of destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי about good things happening on good days, which tells how the לויים were singing when the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוסי says, good things are brought about on a good day, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof. It quotes a ברייתא, and the next step will show how it answers the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words that are left out (the וכו׳) are the important part. That section says the לויים were standing on their platform singing when the first בית המקדש was destroyed. The גמרא will use that singing as evidence.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring about, cause to happen
Merit, a good thing
A good, meritorious day
Etc.: the quote continues beyond what is written

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yosei says:
Good things are brought about on a good day, etc.

steps.raayaObject: The question of whether נסכים alone need שירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי about the day of the חורבן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in step 1.

steps.title: The song must have been over libations
steps.stepSummary: By ruling out every other option, the גמרא concludes that the לויים' song on the day of destruction must have been over נסכים alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was this song for? If it was for an obligatory עולה, was there one? The תמיד had already stopped on the seventeenth of תמוז! If it was for a voluntary עולה, רב מרי taught that a voluntary עולה doesn't need song! So it must have been for נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out what the לויים were singing over. It rules out each kind of קרבן until only נסכים by themselves are left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Obligatory עולות are out, because the תמיד stopped three weeks before תשעה באב. Voluntary עולות are out, because they don't need שירה. The only thing left is נסכים brought alone, so נסכים alone must require שירה.

keyTerms.meaning: An obligatory burnt offering
A voluntary burnt offering
The daily communal offering
The 17th of תמוז, when the תמיד stopped
Rather, is it not...? (introduces the only option left)

phrases.english: This song, what was its purpose?
If you say it was for an obligatory burnt offering,
was there one?
On the seventeenth of Tammuz the daily offering stopped!
Rather, it was for a voluntary burnt offering

phrases.aramaic: — וְהָא תָּנֵי רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
phrases.english: But Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, taught
that it does not require song!
Rather, is it not for libations?

steps.raayaObject: That נסכים brought alone require שירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's report that the לויים were singing, read as process of elimination.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the quoted ברייתא into an actual proof.

steps.title: It was only a lament, not a real Temple song
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רב אשי) rejects the proof. The פסוק the לויים were saying was not even that day's שיר, so they were not performing official שירה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said (some say רב אשי): Do you really think so? The song for that day is 'The earth is ה׳'s and its fullness.' 'And He brought upon them their iniquity' is in Wednesday's song! It was just a lament that came into their mouths.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the proof. The לויים were not singing the official song over any קרבן; they were just crying out words of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חורבן was on מוצאי שבת, which is the first day of the week, and that day's שיר is 'לה׳ הארץ ומלואה.' The פסוק 'וישב עליהם את אונם' belongs to Wednesday's שיר, so it cannot have been the official שירה. Since it was not official שירה, the ברייתא proves nothing about נסכים, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really think so? (rejects an assumption)
The song of the day, the fixed שיר for each weekday
The fourth day of the week, Wednesday
A lament, a cry of mourning

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the day of the חורבן fails. The לויים were lamenting, not performing שירה, so we still do not know whether נסכים alone need שירה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is saying נסכים alone do not need שירה. He only says this ברייתא cannot prove it either way.

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rav Ashi:
And can you really think that?!
The song of that day is "The earth is ה׳'s and its fullness,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 24:1. That day was מוצאי שבת, the first day of the week, whose שיר is this מזמור.

phrases.english: "And He brought upon them their iniquity"
is in the song of Wednesday!
Rather, it was merely a lament
that fell into their mouths.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: וְתִסְבְּרָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the ברייתא, not the possibility that נסכים alone need שירה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the לויים were performing official שירה over a קרבן, but the פסוק was not the שיר of that day, so it was only a spontaneous lament.

steps.title: But the Levites were standing on their platform
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's rejection. The ברייתא says the לויים were standing on their דוכן, which sounds like official שירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says they were 'standing on their platform'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the rejection from Step 4. If the לויים were not doing official שירה, why does the ברייתא say they stood on the דוכן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דוכן is the platform where the לויים stand to sing over the קרבנות. Standing there suggests a formal service, which brings back the proof that שירה was being said over נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform near the מזבח where the לויים stood to sing
It teaches (in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'they were standing on their platform'!
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי from Step 2.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the לויים were not saying official שירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Standing on the דוכן is the sign of official שירה, so the song must have been formal.

steps.title: Levites may sing even without an offering
steps.stepSummary: Following ריש לקיש, the לויים may sing on the דוכן even when there is no קרבן. So standing there does not prove the song was required.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows ריש לקיש, who said: one may say שירה even when it is not over a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by quoting ריש לקיש. The לויים are allowed to stand on the דוכן and sing even when no קרבן is being brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing on the דוכן only shows that they were singing. It does not show that the song was a required part of a קרבן service. So the ברייתא is no proof about נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: The song the לויים sang in the בית המקדש
Not over (not tied to) a קרבן

phrases.english: It is like Reish Lakish,
for Reish Lakish said:
One may say song even when it is not over an offering.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in another אמורא's rule to explain the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Standing on the דוכן means official, required שירה
steps.terutzMaskana: The לויים may sing on the דוכן without a קרבן, so their standing there proves nothing

steps.title: Then let them sing over libations too
steps.stepSummary: If singing without a קרבן is allowed, the לויים should also sing over נסכים that come alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let them also sing over נסכים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about ריש לקיש's rule. If extra singing is allowed, why not sing over נסכים that come alone?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that even if נסכים alone do not require שירה, it should at least be allowed as an optional song. So why would that singing be held back?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Wine poured on the מזבח

phrases.english: If so, let them also say it over libations!
phrases.notes: He means נסכים that come by themselves, without an animal קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what follows from ריש לקיש's rule in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that singing without a קרבן is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If optional singing is allowed, it should be done over נסכים alone too.

steps.title: Singing over libations could lead to a mistake
steps.stepSummary: Optional singing over נסכים alone could cause harm. People might think that singing over נסכים is optional even when they come with a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mishap could come out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the לויים do not sing over נסכים alone. Doing so could cause a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the לויים sang optionally over נסכים alone, people might decide that שירה over נסכים is always optional. They might then skip the required שירה over נסכים that come with a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Will come out of it
A mishap, a bad result

steps.whatToRemember: Standing on the דוכן does not prove official שירה, because of ריש לקיש's rule. So the proof about נסכים alone stays rejected.

phrases.english: A mishap would come out of it.
phrases.notes: The worry is that people would treat the required שירה over נסכים that come with a קרבן as optional too.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical reason (a protective concern)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Optional singing should be done over נסכים alone too
steps.terutzMaskana: It is held back so people do not treat required שירה over נסכים as optional

steps.title: Returning to רבי יוסי's teaching itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to examine רבי יוסי's ברייתא itself: good things happen on good days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רבי יוסי says: Merit is brought about on a meritorious day, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the שירה question and goes back to study רבי יוסי's ברייתא on its own. This sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the ברייתא was used only as a proof about שירה. Now the גמרא looks at its own claims, including that the first חורבן happened in the year after שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: going back to study a source that was quoted earlier
Good things are brought about on a good day

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Yosei says:
Merit is brought about on a meritorious day, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the ברייתא, including that the first חורבן was in the year after שביעית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שירה discussion to study the ברייתא directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: good events happen on good days and bad events on bad days, including the dates of the חורבן

steps.title: A פסוק in יחזקאל puts a יובל fourteen years after the destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא doubts that the first חורבן was in the year after שביעית. A פסוק in יחזקאל places a יובל fourteen years after the destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could the first חורבן really have been in the year after שביעית? But it is written: 'In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the start of the year, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck.' Which year begins on the tenth of the month? It must be יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's dating. It quotes a פסוק in יחזקאל showing that the fourteenth year after the חורבן was a יובל year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a יובל year is counted as starting on the tenth of the month, because יובל begins on יום כיפור. So the year fourteen years after the חורבן was יובל. This fact will be tested against רבי יוסי's date in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The year right after a שמיטה year
Can you find such a case?
The fiftieth year, which begins on יום כיפור
You must say

phrases.english: The first time, in the year after the Sabbatical Year:
can you find such a thing?
But isn't it written:
'In the twenty-fifth year of our exile,
at the start of the year, on the tenth of the month,
in the fourteenth year
after the city was struck'!
Which is the year
whose start is on the tenth of the month?
You must say: this is the Jubilee.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה בְּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית מִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a detail of the ברייתא brought back up in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that the first חורבן was in the year after שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק makes the fourteenth year after the חורבן a יובל, which will not fit that date.

steps.title: The counting does not reach a Jubilee in year fourteen
steps.stepSummary: If the חורבן was in the first year of a שמיטה cycle, the next first year comes at year eight and the one after at year fifteen. So the יובל cannot fall in year fourteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it was destroyed in the first year of the cycle: from one first year to the next first year is eight, and to the first year of another cycle is fifteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge by counting the years. The count shows that רבי יוסי's date and the פסוק in יחזקאל do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יובל comes right after a שמיטה year, so it falls where a 'first year' of a cycle would be. Counting from a first year, the first years come out at years eight and fifteen, not fourteen. So the יובל in year fourteen from the פסוק is impossible on רבי יוסי's dating.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you were to think)
The first year of a seven-year שמיטה cycle
It was destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: Watch how the years are counted. The year of the חורבן itself counts as year one, so the next 'first year' is year eight, not year seven.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that it was destroyed in the first year of the Sabbatical cycle,
from the first year of the cycle to the next first year is eight,
to the first year of another cycle,
it comes to fifteen.
phrases.notes: So the יובל would land in year fifteen, but the פסוק puts it in year fourteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּחַד בְּשָׁבוּעַ חֲרוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from Step 10 by counting the years
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's dating of the first חורבן to the year after שביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting from a first year of the cycle reaches the יובל position at year fifteen, not year fourteen as the פסוק says.

steps.title: רבינא counts the fourteen years from the year after the destruction
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the פסוק means fourteen years after the year of the חורבן. The year of the destruction itself is not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It means in the fourteenth year after the year that the city was struck.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the math problem from Step 11. He rereads the פסוק in יחזקאל so that the fourteen years start counting only after the year of the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, the destruction year was counted as year one, so year fourteen landed on the wrong spot in the שמיטה cycle. רבינא says year one is the year after the חורבן. That pushes everything forward by one year, so the יובל lines up correctly. This keeps רבי יוסי's claim that the חורבן happened in the year after שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: The city was struck, meaning ירושלים was destroyed
After the year; the counting starts after that year ends

phrases.english: Ravina said:
In the fourteenth year
after the year that the city was struck.
phrases.notes: He reads the פסוק in יחזקאל 40:1 closely. The fourteen years start after the destruction year, not with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר שָׁנָה שֶׁהוּכְּתָה הָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting problem raised in Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק so the destruction year is not counted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fourteen years include the year of the חורבן, so the יובל cannot fit
steps.terutzMaskana: The fourteen years begin the year after the חורבן, so the יובל fits a חורבן in the year after שביעית

steps.title: Then the 'twenty-fifth year' would really be the twenty-sixth
steps.stepSummary: If רבינא is right, the same פסוק's phrase 'in the twenty-fifth year of our exile' does not fit, because the count comes out to twenty-six.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how can it say 'in the twenty-fifth year'? It is the twenty-sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא's answer. It points to another number in the same פסוק that would now be off by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל gives two dates for the same event: fourteen years after the חורבן, and the twenty-fifth year of the exile. Adding one year to the first count, as רבינא did, also adds one year to the second count. So the 'twenty-fifth year' becomes twenty-six. The proof for this math comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if we accept what was just said
They come out to; that is the total

phrases.english: If so,
how can it say 'in the twenty-fifth year'?
phrases.notes: These words come from the same פסוק, יחזקאל 40:1, which says 'in the twenty-fifth year of our exile.'

phrases.english: It comes out to twenty-six!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, ״בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה״? עֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ הָוְיָין
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's reading that the fourteen years start after the destruction year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pushing the count forward one year makes the 'twenty-fifth year of exile' in the same פסוק into the twenty-sixth

steps.title: The exile dates prove the count reaches twenty-six
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the years of the exiles. It then adds up the years: eleven, plus fifteen, makes twenty-six.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: They were exiled in the seventh year, they were exiled in the eighth year. They were exiled in the eighteenth year, they were exiled in the nineteenth year. From seven until eighteen is eleven years. Add fifteen, and it comes out to twenty-six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ברייתא that dates the exiles by נבוכדנצר's years of rule. Then it does the math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first exile was in year seven and the חורבן was in year eighteen, which is eleven years apart. Under רבינא's reading, יחזקאל's vision came fifteen years later. That adds up to twenty-six years from the first exile, not twenty-five as the פסוק says.

keyTerms.meaning: They were exiled
Eighteen (Aramaic)
Eleven (Aramaic)
Twenty-six (Aramaic)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא gives two year-numbers for each exile (7 and 8, then 18 and 19). The math here uses 7 and 18. Whether 18 and 19 are really one exile or two is exactly what the next steps argue about, and step 17 settles it.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
They were exiled in the seventh, they were exiled in the eighth.
phrases.notes: These are years of נבוכדנצר's rule. The ברייתא gives two numbers for the first exile.

phrases.aramaic: גָּלוּ בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה, גָּלוּ בִּתְשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.english: They were exiled in the eighteenth, they were exiled in the nineteenth.

phrases.aramaic: מִשַּׁב וְעַד תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי — חַד סְרֵי,
phrases.english: From seven until eighteen is eleven,
and fifteen more makes twenty-six!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: גָּלוּ בְּשֶׁבַע, גָּלוּ בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and the math behind the challenge in Step 13
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבינא's count makes the 'twenty-fifth year' into twenty-six
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא dating the exiles to נבוכדנצר's seventh/eighth and eighteenth/nineteenth years

steps.title: רבינא shows the challenger has the same problem
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the challenger's own count also comes to twenty-six. So the challenger must also leave out the year of the first exile, and רבינא can do the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא could say to you: Does it work out any better for you? They were also exiled in the nineteenth year. From seven to nineteen is twelve years, and fourteen more makes twenty-six! So what must you say? That the year they were exiled is not counted. I can say the same: the year they were exiled is not counted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends himself by showing that the person challenging him gets the same wrong total. Whatever fix the challenger uses, רבינא can use too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenger counts the fourteen years starting from the year of the destruction, but he still reaches twenty-six. The only way out is to leave out the first year of exile from the count of twenty-five. Once that move is allowed, it works for רבינא as well, so the challenge in step 13 no longer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you, by your own view
Does it work out well? Is it any better?
Now, since (opens a reasoning step)
Not counting the year, outside of the year

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not giving up his view here. He is only showing that the challenger needs the same move he does, so his question is not a real problem for רבינא.

phrases.english: Ravina could say to you:
And according to you, does it work out well?
phrases.notes: 'You' is the one who asked in step 13. He counts the year of the destruction as part of the fourteen.

phrases.english: Now, they were also exiled in the nineteenth year;
from seven until nineteen is twelve,
and fourteen more makes twenty-six!
Rather, what do you have to say?
Apart from the year in which they were exiled.
According to me too:
apart from the year in which they were exiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רָבִינָא: וּלְדִידָךְ מִי נִיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 13–14 by showing the challenger faces the same twenty-six count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the question back: the challenger has the same problem, and his fix also works for רבינא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא's way of counting gives twenty-five and twenty-six at the same time, so it cannot be right.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone must leave out the year of the first exile from the twenty-five, so רבינא can do so too.

steps.title: The year nineteen is still a problem for רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses again: even so, the ברייתא's statement that the destruction was in year nineteen still gives רבינא twenty-six years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, 'nineteen' is a difficulty for רבינא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the challenge back. Even after leaving out the year of exile, the number nineteen in the ברייתא does not fit רבינא's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leave out the first exile year (seven) and the destruction year (nineteen). That leaves eleven years in between. רבינא's fourteen years after the destruction, plus the destruction year itself, add fifteen more. That makes twenty-six, not the twenty-five in the פסוק, so the problem from step 14 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, either way
Nineteen (short form of תְּשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה)
It is a difficulty

phrases.english: In any case, 'nineteen' is difficult for Ravina!
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's 'nineteenth year' for the destruction, from step 14. It still adds up to eleven plus fifteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 15 as not fully solving רבינא's problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's view that the fourteen years start after the destruction year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even leaving out the first exile year, the ברייתא's year nineteen gives 11 + 15 = 26, not 25.

steps.title: Only two exiles, counted in two different ways
steps.stepSummary: There were not three exiles but two. The years are counted either from the conquest of יהויקים or from the start of נבוכדנצר's reign, so 'eighteen' and 'nineteen' are the same year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think there were three exiles? They were exiled in the seventh year after the conquest of יהויקים, which is the eighth year of נבוכדנצר. And they were exiled in the eighteenth year after the conquest of יהויקים, which is the nineteenth year of נבוכדנצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining the dates. The numbers that seemed to point to three separate exiles really describe only two, counted with two different calendars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Year seven and year eight are the same first exile. Year eighteen and year nineteen are the same second exile, when the בית המקדש was destroyed. Counting from the conquest of יהויקים, there are eleven years from the first exile to the destruction, leaving out the exile year. Fourteen more gives exactly twenty-five, so רבינא's count works.

keyTerms.meaning: Exiles
The conquest (subjugation) of יהויקים by נבוכדנצר, used as a starting point for counting years
King of בבל, whose own reign was a second way of counting years

steps.whatToRemember: The same events can be dated two ways: from the conquest of יהויקים or from נבוכדנצר's reign. The second count is always one year higher. So year eighteen (from the conquest) and year nineteen (of נבוכדנצר) are one and the same year.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'seventh' and 'eighth', or 'eighteenth' and 'nineteenth', as different events. Each pair is one exile, just dated with a different starting point.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer saves רבינא's reading of the פסוק. It also explains the seeming contradictions between the dates given in different places.

phrases.english: Do you think there were three exiles?
phrases.notes: He means one in year seven or eight, one in year eighteen, and one in year nineteen, as if they were all separate.

phrases.english: They were exiled in the seventh year of the conquest of Jehoiakim,
which is the eighth of Nebuchadnezzar;
they were exiled in the eighteenth year of the conquest of Jehoiakim,
which is the nineteenth of Nebuchadnezzar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 16 by rereading the dates in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the dates: two counting systems, so only two exiles
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Year nineteen was a separate date, which adds an extra year to the count and makes twenty-six.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nineteen of נבוכדנצר is the same as eighteen from the conquest of יהויקים, so the total is twenty-five.

steps.title: A source about נבוכדנצר's first year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins bringing a teaching that lists נבוכדנצר's early years, starting with his conquest of נינוה in his first year. This will support the two-calendar idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: In the first year, he conquered נינוה,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to bring support for its last answer. It quotes a teaching that goes through נבוכדנצר's reign year by year, and this line is only the beginning of the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To prove that the conquest of יהויקים happened after נבוכדנצר's reign had already begun, the גמרא needs a timeline of his early years. Year one is the conquest of נינוה. The next years will show when יהויקים was conquered, which explains why the two counts are one year apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He conquered
The capital of אשור

phrases.english: As the Master said:
In the first year he conquered Nineveh,
phrases.notes: 'He' is נבוכדנצר, in the first year of his reign.
